transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. It's very nice to meet you, too. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Well, I suppose... what made me come in is that my eating has gotten a little, um, all turned around lately. It's probably nothing to worry about, just a silly thing, but some days I just completely forget to eat lunch. And then other days, I'll find myself just standing at the kitchen counter eating crackers and sweets, even though nothing really tastes right. I know I shouldn't be eating like that at my age, I really do try to be good about it. Is that... is that the sort of thing you need to know?
When you eat crackers or sweets at the counter, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you eat?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. It's not like I'm... like I'm gorging myself or anything awful like that. I just have a little nibble here and there, you know? Just a few crackers to settle my stomach, or a little piece of candy because I think it might make me feel a bit brighter. 

I can always stop whenever I want to. I just... sometimes I just don't want to right away. But I'm certainly not out of control. I hope you don't think I'm one of those people who just eats and eats without thinking. That's not me at all. Does that make sense, doctor? I'm trying to be as clear as I can.
Have you been intentionally eating less because you are afraid of gaining weight or because you feel unhappy with your body shape or weight?

Oh, no, no, doctor. It's nothing like that. I know at my age I shouldn't be worrying about being thin like a young girl. I'm perfectly fine with how I look, really I am. 

It's just... well, sometimes I just don't have the appetite, or the food just doesn't seem appealing. It's certainly not because I'm trying to diet or because I think I'm heavy. I try my best to eat sensible meals when I can. I hope that's the right answer... I wouldn't want you to think I'm being vain or foolish about my figure. Is that what you were asking?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day lately?

Well... I suppose I have been feeling a little bit blue, if I'm being perfectly honest. I hope that's alright to say. I try so hard to keep a cheerful face on for everyone, I really do. 

But yes, most mornings lately, I wake up with this... this heavy, low sort of feeling. It's almost like all the color has just drained right out of the day before I even have the chance to get dressed. It's just a silly little mood, I'm sure it's nothing you need to worry too much about. I know I should just count my blessings and pull my socks up, as they say. I do try to shake it off, doctor, I promise I do. Am I explaining that alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right sort of information.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy?

Well... I suppose things have felt a bit different lately. I don't want to sound ungrateful for all the lovely things I have to do. I know I'm very lucky to have my little groups. 

I used to just love my watercolor class... and the quilting circle, and my book club. They were always the highlight of my week. But lately... oh, I feel so terrible admitting this... sometimes I just pack my little tote bag and leave it right by the front door. I just look at it and... I just can't seem to make myself care quite enough to actually go out and do it. 

I know it's awful of me to waste the opportunity, and I always feel so guilty for staying home. I promise I'm going to try harder to get back to them. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around being lazy all day. Do you think it's very bad of me to feel that way, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing.
How long have you been feeling this low?

Oh dear... well, I suppose it's been going on for a little while now. I really hate to admit it, because I know I should have just snapped out of it by now. I really should have. 

It's been... oh, maybe about a year and two months? Yes, I think this low, colorless stretch has been with me for just about that long. I hope you aren't disappointed in me for letting it drag on without saying anything sooner. I really have been trying my very best to stay positive and not be a bother to anyone, I truly have. 

Is that the kind of timeline you needed to know, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting or killing yourself?

Oh, my... that's a very difficult question. I... I want to be honest with you, doctor, because I know you're just trying to help me, and I appreciate that so much. 

I would never, ever do anything to hurt myself. I promise you that. I don't have any sort of plan or anything terrible like that. I know how much that would upset my family, and I could never do that to them. 

But... well, sometimes, when I'm feeling especially like a burden to everyone... I do have this thought that... maybe if I just went to sleep and didn't wake up the next morning, it might just be easier for everyone. A relief, even. It's a dreadful thing to think, I know it is, and I feel so guilty even saying it out loud. I try to push those thoughts right out of my head, I really do. 

I hope you don't think I'm a terrible person for feeling that way sometimes. Is it... is it normal to have silly thoughts like that when you're feeling down? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy most days lately?

Oh, well... I suppose I have been feeling a little bit tired, yes. But really, at my age—I'm 74, you know—I think it's perfectly normal to slow down just a little bit. I certainly don't expect to have the energy of a teenager anymore!

I do try very hard to keep moving and get my little chores done around the house. I make sure the dusting is done and the dishes are put away. I don't want you to think I'm just letting the house fall to pieces. But... yes, I suppose I do need to sit down in my armchair a bit more often than I used to. Sometimes my arms and legs just feel a little heavy, like I've been carrying the groceries for too long, even when I haven't done much at all. 

I'm sure it's nothing to fuss over, though. I really try not to complain about it to anyone. Do you think it's alright that I'm taking a few more rests during the day, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing and not being too idle.
How much have these changes affected your ability to manage your usual daily responsibilities?

Oh, well... I suppose things have slipped just a tiny bit, but really, I’m still managing to stay in my own home, which is the most important thing, isn't it? I’m quite proud of that. I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely helpless. 

But, if I'm being perfectly honest... I did step back from teaching my little craft classes. I just... I didn't want to let anyone down if I wasn't feeling quite up to it, you know? And... oh dear, I feel terrible admitting this... I have missed a few phone calls here and there, and maybe an appointment or two. And some of the little family tasks I used to be so careful about... well, I find myself putting them off just a bit more than I used to. 

I do have to use a lot more little reminder notes now just to keep track of the routine things. I hope that’s alright? I try so hard to keep on top of it all, I really do. I just don't want to be a bother to my family by letting things slide too much. Do you think it's okay to use little notes to help me remember, doctor? I just want to be sure I'm managing things the right way.
